translated: It made me want to get to know her even more deeply.
At the same time, it reminded me how glad I am that Isobe-san is the one playing Saki-chan.
Thank you so much.
That's so kind.
I love the Saki-chan that Isobe-san portrays.
The cold days are continuing, so please take care of yourself.
Thank you for such a thoughtful message.
First of all, hearing you say that makes me so incredibly happy.
It really does.
Thank you.
You're right.
I feel the same way.
Like I mentioned a bit earlier, this time I really tried to empathize with Saki-chan's feelings from many angles.
There was Saki's perspective, and then there was my own perspective
when I first read the script as a reader.
And then there's my professional perspective as a voice actress.
All those things overlapped, and as you wrote, episodes 4 and 8 were truly painful.
During the recording session, how should I put it...
It was like...
Well...
I had to try my best to stay calm, if that's the right way to say it?
Because it felt like my emotions were just going to overflow.
Even with all these different feelings, I had to keep Saki-chan's core in mind.
And...
You mentioned asking about what I was conscious of or what I prioritized.
If I look at it from all those different angles including my own feelings,
then...
It becomes too painful, and my emotions really do just spill over.
But speaking strictly about the recording session, what's most important
is how Saki-chan sees this story, and that's what I focus on as an actress.
